statBlock.name: Blood Elemental
statBlock.classification: Medium Elemental (Water, Mists). Medium size tier shown in header.
statBlock.description: A red mass lashes with its tentacles and leaves a twisting trail that dries in patterns. If it breaks free, it stalks its conjurer and destroys things along the way.

sections.Medium size tier:
Medium elemental (Water, Mists). CR 3. 30 HP (4d8 + 12). Initiative +1. Speed 20 ft..
AC 19, touch 11, flat-footed 18. Base attack +3, grapple +6. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft.
Attack Slam +6 melee (1d8 + 4 plus Blood Drain). Full attack Slam +6 melee (1d8 + 4 plus Blood Drain).
Fort +7, Ref +2, Will +1. Str 16, Dex 12, Con 17, Int 5, Wis 11, Cha 11. Listen +7, Spot +7.
Feats include Power Attack. Advancement 5–7 HD, Medium.
sections.Actions:
Slam. Make one melee slam, or use the full-attack count in the chosen tier. Blood Drain applies to every successful slam against a living creature.
Blood Drain (Ex). After a slam hits a living creature, the elemental attempts to drain its blood as a free action. Fortitude DC equals its HD plus its Constitution modifier. Failure deals 1d4 Constitution damage. The elemental gains 1 HP for each point of Constitution damage actually dealt.
Drench (Ex). Touch extinguishes an exposed nonmagical flame at least one size category smaller than the elemental. Touching magical fire can dispel it as dispel magic at caster level equal to the elemental’s HD.
Engulf (Ex). The elemental can engulf a foe at least one size smaller in a round when it makes no slams. The target can make an attack of opportunity and forgo the save, or decline the attack and attempt a DC 16 Reflex save. An engulfed creature is subject to the 3.5 drowning rules. When an attack hits the elemental, split the damage evenly between it and the engulfed target on a 50% roll if the elemental is one size larger, or 10% if it is two sizes larger. With a gap of three or more categories, only the elemental takes damage.
sections.Traits: Darkvision 60 ft. Immune to poison, sleep, paralysis, stunning, critical hits, and flanking. Does not eat, sleep, or breathe. It cannot be raised or resurrected, though limited wish, wish, miracle, or true resurrection can restore it. Drawn from blood or from water taken from drowned lungs. Exceptionally evil blood can increase its HD. It cannot enter or cross a large body of water. Forced contact with a body of water at least as large as itself deals 1d10 damage each round until it escapes.

sections.Dread elemental rules: Dread elementals understand speech and do not communicate. In Ravenloft, calling a standard elemental has a 20% chance to call a dread elemental instead. Summoning magic always produces the dread forms. An accidental dread elemental is uncontrolled and the Dark Powers supply its materials. Deliberate conjuring uses the matching material and the usual chance to break control. A dismissed dread elemental returns to the fabric of Ravenloft. Its Mists subtype lets it be summoned in any domain and makes it native throughout Ravenloft. The realm’s restrictions on calling do not break the calling pact for these elementals.
sections.Encounter details: Solitary, always neutral evil, no treasure. May appear in any environment.
sections.Drowning: In 3.5, a creature can hold its breath for twice its Constitution score in rounds. Each standard or full-round action uses an additional round of that reserve. Once it runs out, make a DC 10 Constitution check each round, increasing the DC by 1 each round. On a failure it falls unconscious at 0 HP, drops to −1 HP in the following round, and dies in the third.

ruleNotes: Blood Drain uses HD plus Constitution modifier as printed. The DCs in printed tier order are 3, 7, 12, 21, 26, and 29.

Earth Mastery (Ex). Gain +1 to attack and damage while both the elemental and its opponent touch the ground. Against a foe in the air or water, apply −4 instead. The attack lines do not include these modifiers.
Sink (Su, once per hour). Choose one opponent within 60 ft. who is standing on earth or stone. The target makes an opposed grapple check against the elemental. On failure, spectral arms hold it in place. A Medium target sinks to its knees in round 1 and cannot leave its square. If the elemental keeps concentrating, the target sinks to its waist in round 2 and loses its Dexterity bonus to AC. In round 3 it is pulled 6 ft. underground and stays in suspended animation until unearthed. Allies can attempt the 3.5 break another’s pin action to free it before burial.

sections.Actions:
Slam. Make one melee slam, or use the full-attack count in the chosen tier. Each slam deals the indicated bludgeoning and fire damage.
Burn (Ex). A creature hit by the slam makes a Reflex save or burns for 1d4 rounds. Use DC 10 + half the elemental’s HD + its Dexterity modifier. A burning creature can put out the fire with a move action. A creature that hits the elemental with a natural weapon or unarmed strike first takes the slam’s fire damage, then makes the same save to avoid catching fire.
Dance of Death (Su). As a free action, touch a corpse of a formerly living corporeal creature within reach. It rises as a skeleton or zombie according to the corpse’s condition, rushes about attacking creatures and setting fires at random, and adds the effect of a direct hit with alchemist’s fire to its own attacks. That adds 1d6 fire on impact and another 1d6 the following round. A burning target can use a full-round action and a DC 15 Reflex save to extinguish it before that second damage roll. The animated body itself takes 1d3 fire each round until consumed.
sections.Traits: Darkvision 60 ft. Immune to poison, sleep, paralysis, stunning, critical hits, and flanking. Does not eat, sleep, or breathe. It cannot be raised or resurrected, though limited wish, wish, miracle, or true resurrection can restore it. The fire subtype grants fire immunity and cold vulnerability, increasing cold damage by 50%. A pyre belonging to an exceptionally evil person can bring forth an elemental of the next larger size tier even if the caster cannot control it.

ruleNotes: Burn’s explicit DC formula uses Dexterity. The next sentence calls it Constitution-based. Use the explicit formula at the table. The DCs are 12, 15, 19, 25, 28, and 31 in size-tier order. Using Constitution instead gives 11, 14, 17, 22, 24, and 26.
